gem:almeria: Port city under the great Alcazaba and its walls, with the cathedral and Cabo de Gata within 22 km; a good day, plain modern streets.
gem:chelmsford: Essex county city with a cathedral and County Hall; Hylands Park is four kilometres off, but the centre is ordinary.
gem:hardegg: Tiny castle village on the Thaya river inside a national park, with the Vranov chateau across the border; very little else.
gem:maussane-les-alpilles: Provençal village under the Alpilles, with the Barbegal mill, Glanum's arch and Daudet's windmill within 7 km; a pleasant base, little within.
gem:anghiari: Listed hill village with Palazzo Pretorio and a museum of the Battle of Anghiari, Sansepolcro 7 km away; lovely, but soon seen.
gem:roussillon: Hill village in the Plus Beaux Villages list; Sénanque Abbey and the Bories village lie 9 km off, the Pont Julien 4 km.
gem:shrewsbury: Market town with Shrewsbury Abbey, the castle and Ditherington Flax Mill; a good day, though not a long stay.
gem:fordingbridge: Avon market town on the New Forest edge, near Breamore House and Rockbourne Roman Villa; a base rather than a sight.
gem:melilla: Spanish city on the African coast with a historic quarter, fortifications and museums; remote, and a short stay.
gem:brescia: Santa Giulia monastery, two cathedrals and the Palazzo della Loggia, with Lake Iseo near; an industrial city around a fine core.
gem:wissembourg: Alsace border town on the list of Les Plus Beaux Détours de France, with knights' and salt houses and a town hall; small.
gem:saltaire: UNESCO-listed model mill village, a whole planned townscape; compact and quiet, with Bradford's sights five kilometres away.
gem:basford-stoke-on-trent: Stoke-on-Trent suburb near Etruria Hall and its industrial museum, Keele Hall 4 km away; residential, not a reason to go.
gem:hebden-bridge: Market town with its old Picture House and the walk to Stoodley Pike 4 km off; a good day out, few sights.
gem:wittenberg: UNESCO-listed Luther sites: the Castle Church, the Lutherhaus and Melanchthon's house; a plain setting, and the town is small.
gem:liege: Prince-Bishops' Palace, Grand Curtius and La Boverie in a lively Meuse city; much of its fabric is worn and uneven.
gem:eastbourne: Seaside town 4 km from Beachy Head and its lighthouse; the cliffs are the draw, the town is a quiet resort.
gem:subiaco: Sacro Speco, Saint Benedict's monastery built into the cliff, and Saint Scholastica abbey above the Aniene; the town itself is plainer.
gem:veenhuizen: UNESCO-listed village with the national prison museum; a focused half day with little else around it.
gem:mannheim: Grid-plan city with a vast baroque palace, the Kunsthalle and the Wasserturm; postwar streets make it a stopover, not a goal.
gem:tanumshede: UNESCO-listed Bronze Age rock carvings in Tanum; one remarkable site for a few hours, the village itself is plain.
gem:treviso: Compact old city with the Duomo, Palazzo dei Trecento and San Francesco; agreeable for a day, overshadowed by Venice nearby.
gem:ashbourne: Market town with St Oswald's church at the edge of a national park, Ilam Park and Tissington Hall near; a gateway, modest itself.
gem:pienza: UNESCO-listed Renaissance village of Palazzo Piccolomini and its cathedral; tiny, so it fills a day, not a week.
gem:l-escala: Costa Brava town with Cala Montgó and small coves within 4 km; a beach base more than a sight in itself.
gem:kortrijk: Broel towers on the Leie, a belfry and a quiet beguinage; a handsome centre that is done in half a day.
gem:huddersfield: Pennine mill town with a grand railway station and Castle Hill above; little to keep a visitor beyond a few hours.
gem:gradara: Borghi più belli village inside the walls of the Rocca di Gradara, near the Pesaro coast; a few hours inside the walls.
gem:denia: Port town under its castle with long beaches either side; a resort for a beach stay rather than a place to explore.
gem:bayonne: Town of art and history with its cathedral and the Bonnat-Helleu museum, Biarritz's beaches 8 km away; a good day, not a long stay.
gem:hastings: Seaside town with Hastings Castle, two cliff railways, a pier and The Stade fishing beach; an engaging old town amid a tired resort.
gem:pavia: Lombard university city with San Michele Maggiore and San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro; rich Romanesque churches, a quiet day trip.
gem:sabbioneta: A planned Renaissance town with the Teatro all'Antica and Palazzo Ducale inside its walls; very quiet, done in half a day.
gem:cosham: A Portsmouth suburb; HMS Victory and Portchester Castle lie 4 to 6 km away, with nothing of its own to stop for.
gem:fabriano: Marche town named a UNESCO Creative City, with a paper museum and the Frasassi caves 8 km away; a modest centre.
gem:vimbodi: Catalan village 3 km from the UNESCO-listed Poblet Monastery; a base for the abbey, the village itself adds little.
gem:knebel: Coastal village in Mols Bjerge National Park, with hill walks and Kalø castle ruin 7 km off; quiet, little in the village itself.
gem:mamaia-sat: Village behind the Black Sea resort strip with a beach and a few bars; nothing of its own to justify a trip.
gem:brampton: Cumbrian market town with Naworth Castle and an old church; a base for the castles around, not a destination in itself.
gem:saint-etienne: Industrial city and UNESCO City of Design, with the Musée d'Art et d'Industrie and a mine museum; a grey fabric with few sights.
gem:besancon: Cathedral with an astronomical clock and a Roman arch, the Porte Noire, in a stone centre; more handsome than stirring.
gem:jaen: Its cathedral, Arab Baths and provincial museum reward a day; the wider city is ordinary.
gem:wuppertal: Its suspended Schwebebahn railway is unique and the Von der Heydt Museum is good; otherwise a sprawling industrial valley city.
gem:fuengirola: Costa del Sol resort city with Sohail Castle and a long beach; busy and built-up, with few sights beyond the coast.
gem:saint-martin-le-vinoux: Residential suburb of Grenoble; the cathedral and museums on the card belong to Grenoble itself.
gem:winchcombe: Small market town with Sudeley Castle and Hailes Abbey, Cleeve Common walks above; a good day out, quiet in the evening.
gem:faversham: Kent market town with a ruined abbey, the Maison Dieu and a windmill nearby; a pleasant historic stop, not a long stay.
gem:alfriston: Downland village with the Clergy House, a market cross and the Long Man of Wilmington; lovely for a walk, small for a whole day.
gem:franeker: Frisian town around the Eise Eisinga Planetarium, a UNESCO-listed orrery in a house, plus Museum Martena; small and quiet.
gem:le-havre: UNESCO-listed postwar concrete centre around St Joseph's Church, with a beach on the doorstep; striking but austere, a day is enough.
gem:fermo: Hilltop Marche town with the Palazzo dei Priori, the Teatro dell'Aquila and several museums; a good day, quiet after dark.
gem:petronell-carnuntum: Roman Carnuntum, with the Heidentor gate and Museum Carnuntinum, on a UNESCO frontier; the village itself is plain farmland.
gem:aberdeen: Port city with St Machar's Cathedral, the Art Gallery and a long town beach; a solid stop, short on charm.
gem:el-puerto-de-santa-maria: Listed bay town with beaches such as Valdelagrana, across the water from Cádiz; pleasant, but the main sights are in Cádiz.
gem:hexham: Market town around Hexham Abbey, 7 km from Hadrian's Wall; a good base, but the town itself fills half a day.
gem:santa-eularia-des-riu: Island town with its Puig de Missa church and old bridge, beaches close by; a calm base, few sights.
gem:halle-saale: Saale city with a site on the UNESCO tentative list and riverside parks such as the Peißnitz; the card lists few sights, an uneven centre.
gem:san-pedro-alcantara: Costa del Sol resort town with the early Christian basilica of Vega del Mar and beaches; mostly modern holiday sprawl.
gem:aranjuez: UNESCO cultural landscape of royal palace and gardens, the Jardín del Rey and Casa del Labrador; a calm town, a long day trip.
gem:torrevieja: Large Costa Blanca resort city with salt lagoons and a sea museum; mostly a beach base, plain centre.
gem:ceuta: Royal Walls, moat and Monte Hacho on a city beside Africa; a day covers it, with little old fabric beyond.
gem:krinides: Village at UNESCO-listed Philippi with its ancient theatre and the Dikili Tash mound; one major site, nothing else to stay for.
gem:elche: UNESCO palm grove and the mystery play are unlike anything nearby; the modern city around them is plain.
gem:high-wycombe: Buckinghamshire commercial town with a small museum; Hughenden Manor and Cliveden lie nearby, but the centre has little to hold you.
gem:pesmes: Listed village inside its medieval walls, with the Saint-Hilaire church and castle, Acey Abbey 7 km off; an hour or two.
gem:piombino: Industrial port town and ferry gateway to Elba; the listed beautiful village on the card is Populonia, 8 km away.
gem:pontevedra: Galician city in a protected historic grouping, with a walled old town, the Santa María basilica and a museum.
gem:caernarfon: UNESCO-listed Caernarfon Castle and intact town walls, Snowdon and Llanddwyn beach within 16 km; a rewarding day, a small town beyond it.
gem:colchester: Roman Camulodunum with Colchester Castle and the Balkerne Gate; real history, set in an ordinary modern town centre.
gem:cirencester: Cotswold market town with the Corinium Museum and a Roman amphitheatre; a good day and base, not a showpiece.
gem:castel-san-pietro-romano: Listed hilltop village; the Praeneste sanctuary, the Nile mosaic and Palazzo Barberini on its card belong to neighbouring Palestrina.
gem:aylesbury: Buckinghamshire county town with a town hall and the Roald Dahl gallery; Waddesdon Estate lies 7 km out, the centre is plain.
gem:scicli: UNESCO-listed baroque town of churches such as San Bartolomeo and San Matteo; smaller and quieter than its Val di Noto neighbours.
gem:xanten: Lower Rhine town on the UNESCO Lower German Limes, with the Colonia Ulpia Traiana Roman site and St Viktor cathedral; a full day, not more.
gem:keighley: Mill town 5 km from the Brontë Parsonage Museum, with East Riddlesden Hall and Saltaire near; the draws lie around it, not in it.
gem:riomaggiore: Cliff-terraced Cinque Terre village on the UNESCO coast, with Guvano beach 4 km off; steep, busy lanes limit calm.
gem:bridgnorth: Market town with country houses such as Dudmaston and Apley around it; pleasant for a few hours, little to fill a day.
gem:perigueux: Domed Périgueux Cathedral, Renaissance town houses and the Périgord art and archaeology museum; a good day, a gateway rather than a stay.
gem:witten: Ruhr university city with a church, a museum and the Nachtigall industrial museum 3 km away; plain, little to hold a visit.
gem:la-linea-de-la-concepcion: Border town at the gate to Gibraltar, whose caves and museum lie 3 to 6 km away; the town itself offers little.
gem:rochefort: Naval arsenal town with the Corderie Royale, Pierre Loti's house and a transporter bridge; the streets are calm rather than lively.
gem:sunderland: St Peter's Church and the Winter Gardens museum make a short visit; an industrial port city with little to hold a stay.
gem:grosseto: Maremma city with a cathedral, Palazzo Aldobrandeschi and an archaeological museum; a practical base, plain and quiet.
gem:oswestry: Border market town near Whittington Castle; Chirk Castle and the aqueduct lie 7 to 8 km away, with little in town.
gem:taunton: Somerset county town with its castle and the Museum of Somerset, Hestercombe Gardens 4 km out; a working town, a short stop.
gem:naumburg: UNESCO-listed cathedral of St Peter and Paul above an old market town, with Pforta abbey nearby; quiet once the cathedral is seen.
gem:stara-zagora: Bulgarian city with a Neolithic dwellings museum, Roman Augusta Traiana remains and an old mosque; modest, with a plain centre.
gem:sherborne: Sherborne Abbey, the old and new castles and the school's historic library fill a good day; quiet once they are seen.
gem:livorno: Port city with the Fortezza Vecchia, the Duomo and the Fattori museum; lively and genuine, but much of it is plain.
gem:hoek: Small Dutch village whose card carries Leeuwarden's sights and registers; little of its own to visit.
gem:kassel: Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe, the Old Masters gallery and the Fridericianum are real draws; the rebuilt postwar centre is unlovely.
gem:sankt-andreasberg: Harz mining village on a UNESCO list with the Samson mine and museum; the Oderteich lies 7 km away, with the Brocken in view.
gem:nuoro: Sardinian ethnographic and archaeological museums and Grazia Deledda's house, below Monte Ortobene; a plain town around them.
gem:emporeio: Inland Santorini village near Perissa beach and 4 km from Akrotiri; a calmer base, the caldera views are elsewhere.
gem:rochester: Rochester Cathedral, the Guildhall and Restoration House on the Medway; a half day, ringed by plain Medway towns.
gem:craven-arms: Shropshire market village by Stokesay Castle and church with Hopton Castle 8 km off; little in the village itself.
gem:amersfoort: Medieval core with the Koppelpoort water gate, Onze Lieve Vrouwetoren and Mondriaanhuis; a good day, ringed by newer suburbs.
gem:forte-dei-marmi: Tuscan beach resort with a fort and Villa Bertelli, and dunes protected locally; Massa and Seravezza villas lie 6 to 9 km off.
gem:ambleside: Lakeland village by Windermere with Wray Castle, Dove Cottage and fells such as Helm Crag close by; a busy base, small itself.
gem:cremona: Cathedral square with the Torrazzo tower and the baptistery; a fine day on foot, but a plain setting in the Po plain.
gem:grottammare: Listed old upper town with San Giovanni and the battle tower above an Adriatic seaside resort; pleasant for an evening, little more.
gem:frome: Somerset market town with the Blue House, Nunney Castle 4 km and Longleat 6 km off; a pleasant day, few sights in town.
gem:ledbury: Market town with Eastnor Castle on its edge and the Malvern Hills 8 km away; a short visit in itself.
gem:buxton: Spa town of the Crescent, the Devonshire Dome, the Pavilion Gardens and the Opera House; a pleasant day, not a long stay.
gem:bras-sur-meuse: Meuse village 3 km from the Douaumont Ossuary and Verdun forts; the memorials belong to the battlefield, not the village.
gem:nantwich: Cheshire market town with Welsh Row houses, almshouses and an aqueduct; an easy hour, not a destination.
gem:lourmarin: Luberon village in the Plus Beaux Villages list with its Renaissance château; Silvacane Abbey lies 6 km away.
gem:ostersund: Swedish lakeside town on Storsjön with a regional museum and a rune stone on Frösö; a quiet northern base.
gem:halifax: The Piece Hall, the Minster and Shibden Hall give a good half day; a town with little else to hold you.
gem:viareggio: Beach city with the Lorenzo Viani modern art gallery, Villa Puccini and Lake Massaciuccoli near; a seaside stay, few sights of note.
gem:villajoyosa: Listed seaside old town with its walls and Assumption church, beaches on both sides; pleasant for a few hours, modest sights.
gem:tavistock: Market town with its abbey remains, near Buckland Abbey, Cotehele and Morwellham Quay on the moor's edge; a good base, modest itself.
gem:calatayud: UNESCO-listed town of old churches, with the Roman amphitheatre at Bilbilis nearby; modest in size, so a short visit.
gem:voiteur: Jura wine village 6 km from Baume-les-Messieurs abbey and its valley; the village itself has little beyond a short walk.
gem:bolton: Former mill town with a grand town hall, an art museum and Turton Tower nearby; visually plain, little reason to stay.
gem:chichester: Cathedral city with the Market Cross, the Festival Theatre and Fishbourne Roman Palace nearby; a good day, compact and quiet after it.
gem:langemark: Flanders village among the Ypres battlefields, In Flanders Fields museum 7 km away; a base for war memorials, flat and plain itself.
gem:la-roche-guyon: Listed Seine village under its cliff château, with Monet's Giverny 7 km off; a short stop on its own.
gem:orpington: Suburban town on London's edge, near Darwin's Down House and Eltham Palace; the town itself gives no reason to come.
gem:vigo: Large Galician port on the Vigo ria with a cathedral, art museum and Samil beach; busy and working, with a plain centre.
gem:spitz: UNESCO Wachau valley village on the Danube with castle ruins and churches around; a lovely base, but small.
gem:angouleme: Angoulême Cathedral, the château, the town museum and a covered market; a good day, then little to add.
gem:waltham-abbey: Essex market town by Epping Forest and the Lee Valley White Water Centre; outdoor day trips, the town itself is modest.
gem:porto-ercole: Listed harbour village on Monte Argentario, with the Orbetello lagoon and Feniglia dune close by; most named sights lie in neighbouring towns.
gem:udine: City with the Loggia del Lionello, its castle and the Tiepolo galleries in the diocesan museum; a rewarding day, little drama beyond.
gem:forli: Romagna city with the San Mercuriale abbey, Ravaldino fortress and a gallery in San Domenico; solid but not a draw beyond a day.
gem:bautzen: Old town of towers, a cathedral and a town hall above the Spree, with a Sorbian museum; compact, a half day.
gem:san-ildefonso: Royal village of the Palacio de La Granja, its gardens and glass factory, below Peñalara; one grand palace, then the hills.
gem:castel-gandolfo: Listed village above Lake Albano, with the papal summer residence and Lake Nemi 6 km off; little to hold beyond a day.
gem:annelund: Tiny Swedish village whose World Heritage listing belongs to the Engelsberg ironworks four to five kilometres away; the village is quiet.
gem:chippenham: Wiltshire market town five kilometres from Lacock Abbey and Corsham Court; the sights are around it, not in it.
gem:brilon: Sauerland town near the Bruchhauser Steine rocks, 8 km off; fine for walks, with little in the town itself.
gem:arqua-petrarca: Petrarch's house in a listed village of the Euganean Hills, with villas around; quiet and soon seen.
gem:umea: Northern Swedish university city and former Capital of Culture with Bildmuseet; lively with students, but modest to look at.
gem:cheltenham: Regency spa town with Pittville Pump Room, festivals and hills for walking close by; elegant but not distinctive.
gem:bergisch-gladbach: Commuter city by Cologne with Schloss Bensberg and the Altenberger Dom 8 km away; green edges, an ordinary town.
gem:llandudno: Seaside resort below the Great Orme headland with a pier, 5 km from walled Conwy; a good base, dated resort fabric.
gem:auvillar: Listed village with a grain hall, a clock tower and a riverside chapel at its port; lovely for two hours, small for a day.
gem:beynac-et-cazenac: Castle village above the Dordogne with Sarlat 8 km away as a rich second stop; small and often busy.
gem:viterbo: Walled Lazio town around the Palazzo dei Papi and San Lorenzo, with Villa Lante 4 km away; solid heritage, quiet evenings.
gem:montepulciano: Hill town at 605 m with the Palazzo Comunale, the cathedral and San Biagio; a full day, then the countryside.
gem:bishop-auckland: Durham town with Auckland Castle, the Saxon Escomb Church and Binchester Roman Fort; good sights around a tired centre.
gem:henley-on-thames: Thames-side market town with a gallery and houses around it; worth an afternoon, with few sights of its own.
gem:loches: Château, keep and the Saint-Ours collegiate church in a listed art-and-history town; a rewarding half day, quiet in the evening.
gem:sheffield: Former steel city with the Crucible theatre, a cathedral and Park Hill; green edges, but an uneven centre that rarely holds visitors.
gem:senigallia: Adriatic beach town with the Rotonda a Mare pier, the Rocca Roveresca and the Portici Ercolani; pleasant, one of several alike on this coast.
gem:sant-antoni-de-portmany: Ibiza bay town in a protected historic grouping, with Cala Salada 3 km and Cala Comte 7.5 km away; a busy resort feel.
gem:arendal: Skerry-coast town on the Norwegian south coast by a national park, with island churches and a coast museum; few sights of note.
gem:plymouth: Port city with Plymouth Hoe and the Armada Memorial, Mount Edgcumbe 3 km off; beyond the Hoe, the centre is plain.
gem:salou: Beach resort with PortAventura and Ferrari Land on the doorstep; a modern holiday strip with little old character.
gem:sainte-enimie: Listed among France's most beautiful villages, with its old monastery and stone lanes; a rewarding stop, but little to fill a second day.
gem:aquileia: UNESCO-listed Roman site with the Basilica di Santa Maria Assunta and two archaeology museums; a quiet village once the ruins are seen.
gem:reggio-nell-emilia: Emilian city of piazzas, a cathedral and the San Prospero basilica; pleasant streets, but outshone by its neighbours.
gem:karlsruhe: Karlsruhe Palace, the Kunsthalle and the ZKM art and media centre make a good museum day; the city itself is orderly and plain.
gem:bremerhaven: Port city with the German Emigration Center, Klimahaus and a maritime museum; a good museum day, a plain postwar city.
gem:pistoia: San Zeno cathedral, Sant'Andrea and its pulpit, and the Palazzo di Giano make a fine day; not much to hold a second.
gem:pilsrundale: Village around Rundāle Palace and its museum, a grand palace; once the palace is seen, little else holds you.
gem:bobbio: Listed river town with the Ponte Gobbo, the San Colombano museum and a cathedral in the Trebbia valley; a rewarding half day.
gem:knaresborough: Market town under the ruins of Knaresborough Castle, Ripley Castle 7 km away; a good half day, little for longer.
gem:capo-di-ponte: UNESCO rock art parks of Valcamonica anchor this small valley village; beyond the engravings, little else to do.
gem:saffron-walden: Essex market town with Audley End House and Bridge End Gardens; a pleasant day out rather than a stay.
gem:pescasseroli: Mountain village at 1,167 m inside the Abruzzo national park, with Opi and the Barrea lake close; the village itself is modest.
gem:lloret-de-mar: Beach town with coves such as Cala Banys and the Marimurtra garden near; a mass resort with little old character.
gem:riccione: Adriatic beach resort with Villa Mussolini and the Aquafan water park; lively in summer, but one of many alike on this coast.
gem:penzance: Mount's Bay town with the Jubilee Pool, 4 km from St Michael's Mount; a fine base for West Cornwall, the town itself is ordinary.
gem:maidstone: Kent county town with a parish church and castles; Leeds Castle is 8 km away, the centre is ordinary.
gem:lavrio: Old mining port with the ancient theatre of Thorikos and a mineral museum, near Cape Sounion; the town itself is workaday.
gem:bridgwater: Somerset market town known for its carnival; the sights on the card are minor and mostly outside town.
gem:oulchy-le-chateau: Small Aisne village with a Romanesque church and a château; the UNESCO tag does not fit, and little holds a visit.
gem:rugby: Midlands market town known for its school, with a few halls around; little to see and no reason to stay.
gem:pont-aven: Breton heritage village known for its art galleries, the Trémalo chapel close by; a pleasant few hours, little more.
gem:worcester: Worcester Cathedral with its cloister and chapter house, plus the Commandery; the rest of the city is uneven.
gem:church-stretton: Walkers' base below Caer Caradoc in the Shropshire Hills; the small town itself has little beyond its church.
gem:plouharnel: Gateway village to the Carnac stones with beaches close by; the standing stones are mostly in the next town.
gem:lido-di-jesolo: Long Adriatic beach strip of hotels and water parks such as Caribe Bay; nothing old or distinctive to see.
gem:ivanovo: Village by the UNESCO-listed Rock-Hewn Churches of Ivanovo in the Rusenski Lom Nature Park; one remarkable site, little else.
gem:kolding: Koldinghus castle and its museum above a fjord-head city; a good half day, little else to hold you.
gem:mustair: UNESCO-listed Benedictine convent of Saint John in a remote high valley by the Italian border; essentially one great site.
gem:lodi: Lombard town on the plain with a historic centre; the card names little in the town itself, and Milan's lake is the nearest water.
gem:great-malvern: Spa town on the slopes of the Malvern Hills with its Priory; good walking base, a sedate town centre.
gem:lierganes: Stone village of Cantabria with palaces and a historic core, close to the Cabárceno park; the card's zero population is wrong.
gem:clausthal-zellerfeld: Mining town in the UNESCO Upper Harz Water Regale, with its mining museum and Marktkirche; good for a half day, quiet beyond.
gem:gloucester: Cathedral city whose cathedral is the one sight of rank; the rest of the centre adds little.
gem:biella: Textile town with a cathedral and Romanesque baptistery, lakes Sirio and Viverone within 16 km; quiet, and little to stay for.
gem:aschaffenburg: Main-river city with the large Johannisburg palace, the Pompejanum and several museums; solid, but a day covers it.
gem:gabrovo: House of Humour and Satire in town and the Etar open-air museum 8 km off; a good day, with a plain modern centre.
gem:venosa: Basilicata town on the borghi list with an unfinished abbey, an archaeological park and Jewish catacombs; remote and quiet.
gem:skipton: Skipton Castle above a busy market street, with Bolton Priory and Barden Tower near; a gateway town, done in a day.
gem:leek: Market town with All Saints' church, a Brindley water mill and the ruined Dieulacres Abbey; a modest half day.
gem:toro: Listed town with the Colegiata de Santa María la Mayor, an alcázar and a Roman bridge; a good half day, quiet beyond it.
gem:middenbeemster: Village at the heart of the UNESCO-listed Beemster polder, among old windmills; flat and quiet, a few hours by bike.
gem:romsey: Market town around Romsey Abbey, with Mottisfont 6 km off; a pleasant few hours rather than a reason to stay.
gem:saint-remy-de-provence: Provençal town below the Alpilles with the Roman ruins of Glanum and its triumphal arch; a good base, busy and short on depth.
gem:helmsley: Stone market town with Helmsley Castle and Duncombe Park, Rievaulx Abbey 4 km away; a rewarding day, though the town is small.
gem:midhurst: South Downs market town beside the Cowdray Castle ruins and Easebourne Priory; a pleasant stop, short on sights.
gem:worms: Romanesque cathedral of St Peter, the old Jewish cemetery, synagogue and Rashi House; strong history in a plain modern town.
gem:westerham: Small Kent town with Churchill's Chartwell and Quebec House, Darwin's Down House 7 km away; a good half day, small beyond that.
gem:munster: Westphalian city with St.-Paulus-Dom and its astronomical clock, the palace and the historic town hall; a lively, rebuilt core.
gem:colunga: Asturian coast base 3 km from listed Lastres, with Rodiles beach and the Jurassic Museum near; the village itself is plain.
gem:gottingen: University city with a historic observatory, St. Michael's Church and an academy of sciences; a lively but modest old core.
gem:godalming: Surrey market town in the Surrey Hills with the Watts Gallery 4 km away; Guildford's cathedral and castle lie 6 km off.
gem:monpazier: Listed village with its church and Biron castle six kilometres off; a handsome small place, but little fills a stay.
gem:blois: The Royal Castle of Blois and a fine-arts museum above a Loire town of old churches; a full day, not a long stay.
gem:randers: Jutland city known for Randers Regnskov, an indoor rainforest, and an art museum; the centre itself gives little reason to stay.
gem:mitte: Central Hanover with the Neues Rathaus, the Maschsee and the Herrenhausen gardens near; a largely rebuilt centre.
gem:swanage: Dorset seaside town with its pier; Old Harry Rocks lie 4 km away and Corfe Castle 8 km, so it works as a base.
gem:triora: Listed stone village at 780 m below Mont Saccarel and Monte Ceppo; a half day unless you hike.
gem:arundel: Arundel Castle, the cathedral and the Fitzalan Chapel in a small market town; a half day covers it.
gem:helsingborg: Øresund port city with the Kärnan tower and Sofiero palace, Helsingør a ferry hop away; pleasant, but its best sights are across the water.
gem:guildford: Surrey city with a castle, a modern cathedral and Abbot's Hospital, and the Surrey Hills 6 km away; handsome and commuter-busy.
gem:halver: Sauerland edge town with the Karlshöhe lookout tower and reservoirs nearby; green hills, but nothing to travel for.
gem:tabor: Hussite-era hilltop town with its Kotnov castle and a geopark nearby; compact, with a few sights spread around.
gem:solothurn: Swiss town with a cathedral, an art museum and the Weissenstein ridge close by; compact, with a short list of sights.
gem:burnley: Mill town with Towneley Park, a textile mill museum and Gawthorpe Hall 4 km off; little beauty in the town itself.
gem:noli: Listed seaside village with the Romanesque church of San Paragorio and a beach, the Bergeggi reserve close by; small, busy in summer.
gem:ingolstadt: Danube city with the Liebfrauenmünster, the Asam church of Maria de Victoria and the Audi museum; a day, no more.
gem:bewdley: Severn town with Bewdley Bridge and the West Midland Safari Park; a pleasant riverside stop, not a full day.
gem:darlington: Railway town with the Skerne Bridge and the Roman bridge at Piercebridge nearby; plain streets and little to hold a visitor.
gem:monmouth: Wye valley market town with its fortified bridge gatehouse, Castle House and Puzzlewood nearby; a pleasant day, not more.
gem:castro-urdiales: Historic harbour town with the Santa María church and Santa Ana castle above the port; a fine half day on a busy coast.
gem:mellie-a: Hilltop town over Golden Bay and Għajn Tuffieħa, with Popeye Village and Comino's Blue Lagoon close; a beach base, little old fabric.
gem:morpeth: Northumberland market town with a clock tower, a castle gatehouse and Newminster Abbey ruins; agreeable, but one of many.
gem:zamora: Walled old town with its cathedral, San Vicente and the Momos palace; a rewarding day, quiet beyond it.
gem:chagford: Moorland market village with Castle Drogo and Spinsters' Rock 3 km away; a good walking base, small for a full day.
gem:saarbrucken: Saarland capital with the baroque Ludwigskirche and Saarbrücken Castle; a few good buildings in an uneven postwar city.
gem:hereford: Cathedral city with its cathedral green and the Old House museum; a good half day, the rest of the city is ordinary.
gem:wetzlar: Hessian city with a cathedral, the old imperial court and Goethe-linked houses; compact, with little beyond them.
gem:noyers: Listed Burgundy village of intact medieval houses and gates beside a river bend; very small, a short visit.
gem:ruddington: Commuter village south of Nottingham; the castle and museums on the card all lie in the city.
gem:royal-tunbridge-wells: Spa town with theatres, Penshurst Place and Groombridge Place nearby; genteel and comfortable, but its best sights are outside.
gem:siofok: Lake Balaton resort town with beaches and the Kálmán Imre museum; sights are thin and the place is built for summer stays.
gem:siano: Small Calabrian hill village; the card lists only sights of nearby Catanzaro, so little of its own is shown.
gem:folkestone: Cliff-top Leas promenade, a Roman villa and coastal country parks nearby; a pleasant walk, but a worn town centre.
gem:biot: Riviera hill village with Sainte-Marie-Madeleine church, the Picasso Museum and Fondation Maeght 6 to 8 km off; small on its own.
gem:le-mans: City with a great cathedral and an old quarter around Place Saint-Michel and the Psalette; the rest of the city is plain.
gem:castello-de-la-plana: Provincial city with a cathedral, the El Fadrí bell tower and a fine-arts museum; beaches lie outside and the centre is soon seen.
gem:oundle: Stone market town ringed by castles and halls such as Fotheringhay and Barnwell; pleasant for a half day, little more.
gem:dorchester: Hardy country: Max Gate, a Roman town house and Maiden Castle hillfort nearby; the county town itself is ordinary.
gem:estepona: Costa del Sol town with a small castle and watchtowers along the shore; a beach stay, one resort among many.
gem:osnabruck: Cathedral, town hall and the Felix Nussbaum museum in a large, compact old centre; solid, not a standout.
gem:knokke: Smart Belgian seaside resort with art galleries, a casino and the Zwin reserve close by; a built-up beachfront with little old character.
gem:carlisle: Border city with a cathedral precinct and the Tullie House museum; a worthwhile stop, too little for a stay.
gem:chorley: Lancashire market town with a hall and a church; the sights listed lie in neighbouring villages, not in town.
gem:coventry: The bombed and new cathedrals of St Michael and stretches of city wall in a city rebuilt after the war; much plain postwar fabric.
gem:settle: Dales market town with Victoria Cave in the limestone above and an old bridge; a good walking base, little to see in town.
gem:wigan: Former mill town with Haigh Hall and its parish churches; plain urban fabric and no reason to stay.
gem:medinaceli: High walled village with a Roman triple arch and ducal palace; very small, done in half a day.
gem:scarborough: Seaside town with a headland castle, the Rotunda Museum and St Mary's church; faded resort streets between the bays.
gem:prato: Castello dell'Imperatore, the cathedral with Donatello's pulpit and a textile museum; a rewarding day, inside a sprawling industrial city.
gem:zdar-nad-sazavou: Town with the UNESCO-listed pilgrimage church of Saint John of Nepomuk and the Žďár monastery; one remarkable church, an ordinary town.
gem:cluny: Remains of the great abbey of Cluny, with a European Heritage Label, in a small old town; much of the abbey is gone.
gem:kecskemet: Plains city with an ornate city hall, the Cifrapalota and a photography museum; a pleasant few hours, little scenery.
gem:greve-in-chianti: Chianti market village with Verrazzano castle and Passignano abbey within 6 km; a good wine-country base, little to see in town.
gem:ostrava: Industrial city with the Michal Mine, Silesian Ostrava Castle and a lively theatre; visually rough, more interest than beauty.
gem:abergavenny: Welsh market town below the Blorenge with a castle, near the Blaenavon industrial landscape; a good walking base.
gem:radevormwald: Upland town among reservoirs such as the Bevertalsperre, with a railway museum nearby; little that draws a visitor.
gem:lindlar: Bergisches Land town with an open-air museum and moated castles around; a family outing, not a destination.
gem:berwick-upon-tweed: Border town on the Tweed with castle remains, a railway station and the Union Chain Bridge 7 km away; quiet outside the walls.
gem:ruthin: Welsh market town of old timbered houses such as Nantclwyd y Dre, with a castle, near Moel Famau; a pleasant half day.
gem:warwick: Castle town around Warwick Castle with Kenilworth Castle 7 km and Leamington Spa 3 km away; strong for a day, then spent.
gem:meschede: Hill-country town with Königsmünster Abbey and reservoirs such as the Hennesee near; a base for walks, little in town.
gem:alcoy: Hill city with modernist houses such as Casa del Pavo and the Llotja de Sant Jordi; a half day, uneven beyond.
gem:sos-del-rey-catolico: Listed walled hill village with the Santa Feliciana castle and the Sada palace; a rewarding half day, quiet after that.
gem:fira: Caldera-rim town on Santorini with the volcanic basin below, plus two museums; busy and commercial once off the edge.
gem:terracina: Lazio coast town with the Cattedrale di San Cesareo and a Roman theatre in its upper town; a good half day by the sea.
gem:soria: Listed upland town at 1,064 m with the San Juan de Duero cloister, San Pedro and the Numantine Museum; quiet, a day covers it.
gem:blackpool: Blackpool Tower, the piers and the Pleasure Beach rides make a loud seaside day; little beauty in the town's fabric.
gem:roses: Costa Brava bay town with Cap de Creus park 5 km away and Sant Pere de Rodes monastery 7 km off; summer-led.
gem:frantiskovy-lazne: Neat spa village among the Great Spa Towns of Europe, Cheb Castle 4 km away; restful but quiet, a day is enough.
gem:otley: Wharfedale market town under the Chevin ridge; good walking, few sights of its own.
gem:ayr: Seaside town with a beach and town hall, the Brig o' Doon 4 km off; plain streets, little to hold a visitor.
gem:a-guarda: Fishing town under the Castro de Santa Trega hillfort at the Miño mouth; Caminha's sights lie across the river.
gem:grassington: Stone Dales village by Grassington Bridge on the Wharfe, with Barden Tower and Burnsall close; a base for walks rather than sights.
gem:aberystwyth: Welsh seaside university town with a castle ruin, Old College and beaches; lively in term time, modest sights.
gem:wolverhampton: Black Country city with St Peter's church and an art gallery, near Wightwick Manor; visually plain, little reason to stay.
gem:landshut: Bavarian city with Burg Trausnitz above a Gothic core around the Basilika St. Martin; handsome, but a day covers it.
gem:newton-abbot: Devon market town with Bradley Manor and Forde House, Torquay 9 km away; a working town, the coast is the draw.
gem:pezenas: Hérault town in the Plus Beaux Détours list with a collegiate church organ and the Pénitents Blancs sacristy; a compact old core.
gem:astorga: Walled heritage town with Gaudí's Episcopal Palace, a cathedral and the Camino museum; compact, a half day to a night.
gem:paignton: Seaside resort with Goodrington Sands, the zoo and the steam railway; the town itself is a plain holiday strip.
gem:savona: Ligurian port city with the Priamar fortress, Palazzo Della Rovere and a cathedral; handsome in parts, overshadowed by Genoa.
gem:clitheroe: Lancashire market town with a castle, and Whalley and Sawley abbeys five to six kilometres away; a gentle stop, not a destination.
gem:vallon-pont-d-arc: Gateway to the Ardèche gorges, 3 km from the Pont d'Arc with the Grotte Chauvet 2 replica; a strong base, the village is touristy.
gem:sutomore: Montenegrin beach village with Ratac Abbey and King Nikola's Palace 6 km away, Lake Skadar farther; a summer-led stop.
gem:fontenay-le-comte: Renaissance mansions and the Notre-Dame spire around Place Belliard; a pleasant stop, not enough for a full day.
gem:perth: Scottish town with St Ninian's Cathedral and a city hall; Scone Palace is three kilometres off, and Elcho Castle five.
gem:benevento: Arch of Trajan, Roman theatre and the Santa Sofia complex in a Campanian city; strong sights in an uneven, little-visited centre.
gem:diksmuide: First World War town with the Yser Tower and a UNESCO listing, beaches 17 km away; rebuilt and quiet, half a day.
gem:berkhamsted: Market town with Berkhamsted Castle ruins and nearby parkland; pleasant but ordinary, with little to fill a day.
gem:orebro: Örebro Castle and the Svampen water tower; a pleasant walk of a few hours, not a reason to travel.
gem:luneburg: Brick-Gothic salt town with St. Johannis, the old harbour crane and the salt museum; compact, done in a day.
gem:devizes: Market town with a castle, market cross and the Kennet and Avon Canal Museum; worth a stop, little for a full day.
gem:beroun: Town in a UNESCO geopark of karst cliffs, with the Koněprusy Caves 5 km off; the town itself holds little for a day.
gem:hawes: Dales market village with a countryside museum and Gayle Mill in the Yorkshire Dales park; scenic, but small.
gem:armagh: Cathedral city with St Patrick's Cathedral and county museums, and Navan Fort listed nearby; small, quiet, with a short list of sights.
gem:much-wenlock: Small market town 6 km from the Iron Bridge and Blists Hill, with Benthall Hall close; the big sights are in the gorge.
gem:kirkby-stephen: Small market town with Brough and Pendragon castles 6 km off; a stop on the way, little in the town.
gem:chinon: Royal fortress above a listed old town of townhouses; a rewarding half day, quiet in the evening.
gem:rovereto: The MART modern art museum and the Italian War Museum, with Castel Beseno near; a tidy town that is seen in a day.
gem:kiel: Baltic port city with a shipping museum, Moenkeberg beach and Kiel Castle; a modern, workaday centre with little old fabric.
gem:tarnowskie-gory: UNESCO-listed historic silver mine with an adit and shafts around town; a niche day for mining heritage.
gem:bromley: Outer London town with Eltham Palace and Down House within 9 km; Greenwich's sights are 8 km away, little of its own.
gem:langport: Small market town with its Hanging Chapel and Muchelney Abbey near, wet moors all around; quiet, and an hour or two suffices.
gem:sanremo: Riviera resort with its casino, Villa Nobel and a Roman villa on the shore; pleasant for a night, the town is largely modern.
gem:fulwood: Leafy Sheffield suburb whose listed sights all lie in the city 6 to 7 km away; a place to sleep, not to visit.
gem:villena: Historic town under the Atalaya castle, home of the Treasure of Villena; a short visit, the town around is plain.
gem:medebach: Small Sauerland town with its parish church, wooded hills around and the Edersee 21 km away; for walkers, little in town.
gem:de-panne: Belgian beach resort at the French border with Oostduinkerke and Nieuwpoort beaches near; Veurne's market square lies 6 km off.
gem:paderborn: City with a cathedral, the Kaiserpfalz museum and the Heinz Nixdorf computer museum; a solid day, plain apart from its core.
gem:menerbes: Listed hill village near Lacoste castle, Goult and the Village des Bories; a rewarding half day, few sights inside.
gem:toulon: Naval port under Mont Faron with the Mourillon beaches and the Tour Royale; a working city with an uneven centre.
gem:bishops-stortford: Hertfordshire market town with castle remains, near Hatfield Forest and Stansted; a commuter town, not a destination.
gem:wiesbaden: Elegant spa city with the Nerobergbahn, the Marktkirche and Museum Wiesbaden; polished, but a day covers it.
gem:marsberg: Sauerland town with the Buttenturm and the old upper town, Bredelar monastery 7 km off; little to detour for.
gem:kudowa-zdroj: Spa town with the Chapel of Skulls, a base for the Błędne Skały and Szczeliniec rock mazes; the town itself is modest.
gem:wattwiller: Vosges foothill village below the Hartmannswillerkopf battlefield memorial; a base for walks, little to see in the village itself.
gem:cesenatico: Adriatic resort with a canal port and a maritime museum; pleasant for a summer stay, one of many along this coast.
gem:liberec: Town hall and castle in the centre, the Ještěd tower on its peak 6 km off; an uneven city around a handsome core.
gem:otterlo: Doorstep base for the Kröller-Müller Museum 3 km away and the Veluwe heath; the village itself is plain.
gem:sainte-suzanne: Listed fortified village with a castle, ramparts and a dolmen nearby; a good stop of two hours, quiet beyond that.
gem:zernez: Engadine village with the Swiss National Park centre, ringed by peaks such as Piz Nuna; a walking base, little to see in the village.
gem:aosta: Roman arch, theatre and forum cryptoporticus under Alpine peaks; compact, so a day or two is plenty.
gem:albacete: Large La Mancha city with a cathedral and a cutlery museum; a fair-sized, historic-listed centre, but plain and quickly seen.
gem:evesham: Market town with the Evesham Abbey site, Abbot Reginald's Gateway and two old churches; a pleasant half day, little more.
gem:biel-bienne: Bilingual watch city on Lake Biel with a lido, Nidau castle and the Taubenloch gorge; pleasant, but a stop rather than a reason to go.
gem:bedford: River Great Ouse town with a castle mound and St Paul's church; a pleasant embankment, but nothing that draws a trip.
gem:kington: Quiet Herefordshire market town with a museum and Hergest Ridge walks close by; little beyond a pleasant stop.
gem:bova: Listed hill village at 820 m with a co-cathedral; little to see beyond a short walk.
gem:lark-hill: Village on the card beside Stonehenge; the stones are the draw, the village itself offers nothing to stay for.
gem:swindon: Railway town with the STEAM museum, Barbury Castle and white horses on the downs nearby; the town itself is visually unrewarding.
gem:plasencia: Walled Extremadura town with an old and a new cathedral side by side; a rewarding few hours, quiet beyond the centre.
gem:natzwiller: Home of the Natzweiler-Struthof camp memorial, a sober half day; the village offers nothing else to stay for.
gem:hathersage: Peak District village in the Derwent valley with a stone circle and Peveril Castle nearby; a walking base, few sights in the village.
gem:lignano-sabbiadoro: Big Adriatic beach resort among pine woods at the mouth of the Tagliamento; a beach holiday, no character beyond it.
gem:magdeburg: Elbe city with a great Gothic cathedral and the Romanesque Kloster Unser Lieben Frauen; much of the centre is postwar and plain.
gem:bad-schandau: Elbe spa village amid Saxon Switzerland's table mountains, with the Bastei and Königstein Fortress within 8 km; a good base, small in itself.
gem:sisteron: Citadel and town walls above the Durance, with a Romanesque cathedral below; a rewarding half day on the road south.
gem:mangalia: Coastal town with the Esmahan Sultan mosque and Callatis museum; the resort beaches nearby are the main draw.
gem:cottbus: Lusatian city with the Branitz park 3 km out, a Wendish museum and a fine state theatre; pleasant, but quickly done.
gem:luso: Spa village at the foot of the Buçaco forest, with its convent and military museum; a rewarding half day, the village is plain.
gem:brandenburg-an-der-havel: Havel city with a cathedral hill, the old town hall and medieval gate towers; lakes lie 3 to 8 km off.
gem:leiria: Castle above a river city with a cathedral and market; a lively regional centre, but modest as a destination.
gem:matalascanas: Beach resort at the edge of Doñana, with the Torre de la Higuera on the sand; a gateway to the park, plain itself.
gem:newark-on-trent: Market town with a castle and church on the Trent; pleasant to pass, though the listed sights lie several kilometres out.
gem:savoca: Sicilian hill village in the Borghi più belli list with the Norman church of Santi Pietro e Paolo d'Agrò; very small.
gem:oia: Santorini village on the caldera above Amoudi Bay, the island's views at its feet; small, and best seen in a few hours.
gem:divaca: The UNESCO Škocjan Caves are the reason to come; the village is a small base with little else.
gem:szczawnica: Pieniny spa village at the Dunajec river gorge, under the Three Crowns peak; a busy resort strip in season.
gem:coningsby: Lincolnshire village beside Tattershall Castle's brick keep; one sight for an hour or two, flat country around.
gem:messina: The Duomo with its astronomical clock, the Orion fountain and the regional museum fill half a day; the wider city is ordinary.
gem:vasteras: Lakeside city with a cathedral, castle and a restored power station museum; solid but lacking a strong draw.
gem:ootmarsum: Small Twente village with Singraven watermill 6 km and a megalithic tomb 7 km away; quiet, with little for a second day.
gem:egersund: Small port town in the Magma UNESCO Geopark with a church and lighthouse nearby; a short stop on the coast.
gem:st-austell: Clay-country town by the Eden Project and the Wheal Martyn clay museum; come for Eden, the town itself is plain.
gem:pomorie: Bulgarian Black Sea town beside Pomorie Lake with a monastery of St. George; Sunny Beach lies 15 km off, sights are few.
gem:blaenavon: Former iron town at the core of the UNESCO Blaenavon Industrial Landscape, with its ironworks and the Blorenge above; a half day.
gem:saintes-maries-de-la-mer: Camargue seaside village with a pilgrimage church, a bullring and bird park near; beach and nature are the draw, sights are few.
gem:solingen: City with Müngsten Bridge 4 km off and Schloss Burg 6 km; little worth seeing in the centre itself.
gem:taggia: Listed medieval town above the Riviera coast with the convent of San Domenico, Sanremo 7 km away; pleasant for half a day.
gem:achicourt: Suburb on the edge of Arras; the cathedral, citadel and town hall on the card belong to Arras, the village itself has little.
gem:bestwig: Sauerland town amid forest with an abbey and small castles around; spread over several villages and quiet.
gem:chepstow: Border town above the Lower Wye Gorge with its old Wye Bridge, the Severn Bridge close by; a good valley start, a short stay.
gem:palazzuolo-sul-senio: Small listed Apennine village with a couple of churches and a mountain-life museum; fine for a quiet stop, not more.
gem:logrono: Listed old quarter around the co-cathedral of La Redonda and Santa María de Palacio; agreeable streets, but few sights for a second day.
gem:vilanova-i-la-geltru: Catalan coastal city with five museums, including the railway museum, and beaches; a pleasant day trip, no strong centre.
gem:landore: Industrial district of Swansea, its listed sights such as Swansea Castle and the Glynn Vivian gallery in the city centre; no draw of its own.
gem:carucedo: Small village 3 km from the Roman gold mines of Las Médulas, with Cornatel castle near; a base for the site, little of its own.
gem:zwolle: Old centre with the Sassenpoort gate and the Broerenkerk; a pleasant day, few sights of wider rank.
gem:cambrai: Town with a UNESCO listing, a cathedral, two béguinages and old ramparts; worth a few hours, flat and plain beyond the core.
gem:chesterfield: Market town known for the Holy Trinity and its church spire, Bolsover Castle 8 km off; plain beyond the centre.
gem:margate: Kent seaside town with the Shell Grotto and a sandy front; a fun day out, frayed resort fabric around it.
gem:foligno: Flat Umbrian city with the San Feliciano cathedral and frescoed Palazzo Trinci; Spello is 5 km away, the city itself is workaday.
gem:enniskillen: Island town on Lough Erne with its castle and Devenish Island's monastic site 3 km off; a good base, a modest town.
gem:la-manga-del-mar-menor: Resort strip on a sand bar between the Mar Menor and the sea, facing Isla Grosa; high-rise holiday blocks with little character.
gem:gelsenkirchen: Ruhr city of football and mining, with the Zollverein colliery 4 km away in Essen; the town itself offers little beauty.
gem:stony-stratford: Old coaching market town on the edge of Milton Keynes, near the Cosgrove aqueduct; pleasant high street, little to see.
gem:carrara: Marble city below the Apuan Alps, with the Fontana del Gigante and the Sant'Andrea collegiate church; the centre is small and worn.
gem:vir: Island holiday village with small beaches such as Jadro; no named sight of note and a spread of holiday houses.
gem:clermont-ferrand: Cathedral city with the Puy de Dôme volcano within 10 km; the centre holds about a day of sights.
gem:almunecar: Costa Tropical resort with San Miguel Castle above town beaches and the Maro-Cerro Gordo cliffs nearby; holiday blocks dilute the old core.
gem:balatonfured: Lake Balaton resort town with a promenade and the Tihany peninsula and abbey 6 km away; summer-led, quiet in winter.
gem:hillsborough: County Down village built around Hillsborough Castle; one stately visit, little more to hold the day.
gem:rothbury: Northumberland village with the Cragside estate and Brinkburn Priory close by, a good base for the hills; small and quiet.
gem:macerata: Marche hill town with the Sferisterio arena, Palazzo Buonaccorsi and the Palazzo Ricci museum; a good day, little beyond it.
gem:gavle: Swedish city with a castle, the Gävle goat and a railway museum; a modest centre that holds little beyond a few hours.
gem:manilva: Costa del Sol town of resorts and coastal watchtowers, near the Roman site of Lacipo; ordinary beaches, little to explore.
gem:southampton: Port city with the Bargate, Tudor House and the SeaCity museum, Netley Abbey 4 km off; a modern centre with little charm.
gem:tortosa: Ebro town with a cathedral, a Gothic exchange hall and the Túbal tower; historic and quiet, a good half day.
gem:roissy-en-france: Village wrapped by Paris-CDG airport, with Le Bourget's Air and Space Museum 9 km away; a place to sleep before a flight.
gem:kempten-allgau: Allgäu city with the Residenz, the old abbey and the Basilica of St. Lorenz; a solid day, not a city for long.
gem:southport: Seaside town with the Wayfarers Arcade and the Atkinson arts centre, Formby beach ten kilometres off; faded rather than compelling.
gem:ciutadella: Menorca's historic port town with its cathedral and listed old quarter, coves such as Cala Mitjana nearby; busy in high summer.
gem:lorsch: UNESCO-listed Carolingian abbey gatehall in a small Hessian town; a distinctive single sight, with little else around.
gem:bonn: Beethoven's birthplace on the Rhine, with a minster and strong museums; refined but modest in scale for a large city.
gem:bellaria-igea-marina: Adriatic beach resort near the Rubicon, its named sights in towns 4 to 9 km away; a beach stay, little to see.
gem:gruiten: Small village between Düsseldorf and Wuppertal, near the Neander valley and the Schwebebahn; a local outing, not a trip.
gem:hyeres: Old town, Villa Noailles and Port-Cros National Park 8 km away give a Riviera base; sprawl lessens the centre.
gem:kardzhali: Rhodopes town with a regional history museum and Vishegrad fortress 5 km out; a plain centre that serves as a stop.
gem:linkoping: Large city with a big cathedral and the county museum; the rest is quickly seen.
gem:wakefield: West Yorkshire city with a cathedral, a theatre and Sandal Castle; Nostell Priory lies 8 km off, the centre is ordinary.
gem:lisburn: Belfast satellite city with its cathedral and the Giant's Ring and Hillsborough Castle within 8 km; little reason to base here.
gem:sambuca-di-sicilia: Listed Sicilian hill village with the Adranone ruins and the Mazzallakkar fort a few kilometres off; a couple of hours, little more.
gem:szilvasvarad: Village by the Szalajka spring, with caves and the Bélapátfalva abbey nearby; good for walks, small.
gem:poitiers: Romanesque Notre-Dame la Grande, the Baptistère Saint-Jean and the ducal palace hall; a pleasant student city, not a long stay.
gem:lovere: Listed lakeside village on Lake Iseo with an art museum and a cathedral; lovely setting, though small.
gem:le-cap-d-agde: Modern Mediterranean resort, with Agde's cathedral 5 km away; beaches and marinas, no old fabric of its own.
gem:campiglia-marittima: Listed hill village with its Rocca and the San Silvestro mining park below; a half day, with the coast 7 km off.
gem:montefalco: Listed Umbrian hilltop village with the San Francesco museum; many named sights are in Foligno 9 km off, so a half day here.
gem:newbury: Berkshire market town with a museum, corn exchange and Highclere Castle 9 km away; solid but unremarkable.
gem:neath: Valley town with a castle ruin and Victoria Gardens, Gower beaches 16 km away; little to bring a visitor here.
gem:fulda: Baroque cathedral of St Salvator, the Michaelskirche and the Stadtschloss; a rewarding day, quiet beyond the quarter.
gem:dalby: Skåne village with the Dalby Söderskog national park woods and the Holy Cross church; a short outing, little more.
gem:ligourion: Village 4 km from the theatre and Asclepius sanctuary of Epidaurus; a handy bed, but the site is not the village.
gem:jyvaskyla: Lakeside university city with Alvar Aalto buildings and museums; pleasant, but compact, with a modern centre.
gem:market-drayton: Shropshire market town with a memorial cross; Styche Hall and the Blore Heath battlefield lie 3 to 4 km out.
gem:betws-y-coed: Snowdonia village among wooded valleys, near Gwydir Castle and Tŷ Hyll, with Snowdon in reach; a walking base, busy in season.
gem:josselin: Breton heritage town with its castle and the Notre-Dame du Roncier basilica; a fine half day, little to keep you longer.
gem:monchengladbach: Museum Abteiberg, Schloss Rheydt and the abbey church stand out in an otherwise plain industrial city.
gem:szekesfehervar: Hungarian city with a cathedral basilica and a ruin garden of the old royal church; low-key, a day trip from Budapest.
gem:eslohe: Sauerland town with a machine museum and village churches in wooded hills; a quiet base, little to see.
gem:reading: Thames-valley business city with abbey ruins and Forbury Gardens; the sights are few for a city of this size.
gem:macclesfield: Market town with old churches and the White Nancy folly on the hill nearby; little to hold a visitor for a day.
gem:chatillon-sur-seine: Burgundy town in the Plus Beaux Détours list with Saint-Vorles church and a regional museum; the card names no standout.
gem:kingston-upon-hull: Ferens Art Gallery, Wilberforce House and the Minster in an estuary port; worthwhile museums in an unlovely city.
gem:potes: Stone town of Liébana with the Torre del Infantado, near Santo Toribio and the Picos de Europa; a fine base, the town itself is small.
gem:ponte-arche: Valley village in a UNESCO biosphere reserve, the Brenta group 14 km and Lake Molveno 12 km away; a base, little in the village.
gem:santa-teresa-gallura: Sardinian port by Rena Bianca beach and the granite of Capo Testa, facing the Maddalena islands; a resort town, thin on character.
gem:derby: Midlands city with the Museum of Making and a cathedral, Kedleston Hall nearby; useful museums, an unremarkable centre.
gem:kielce: Regional city with the Palace of the Kraków Bishops, a cathedral and the Kadzielnia quarry park; a plain centre, quickly done.
gem:coburg: The vast Veste Coburg above a ducal town with Schloss Ehrenburg and Rosenau nearby; a rewarding day, little beyond it.
gem:apsley: Hertfordshire commuter village with St Albans Cathedral 9 km and Berkhamsted Castle 7 km away; nothing much in the village.
gem:santo-stefano-di-sessanio: Stone hill village in a national park, with Rocca Calascio castle four kilometres off; tiny, so best as an overnight.
gem:huntingdon: Cambridgeshire market town with a Cromwell museum and Houghton Mill 4 km away; pleasant, modest, little to hold a day.
gem:arevalo: Listed Castilian town with the La Lugareja hermitage, a castle and the Medina bridge; a good stop of a few hours, quiet otherwise.
gem:pravia: Historic-listed Asturian town with a church and a mining ecomuseum; beaches and the Candamo cave lie six to nine kilometres away.
gem:llandeilo: Small town by Dinefwr Castle and park, with Carreg Cennen and Aberglasney 5 km off; a good base, little in town itself.
gem:stafford: Staffordshire county town with a castle ruin; the grander houses on the card lie some kilometres outside.
gem:chioggia: Lagoon fishing town of canals and a lively waterfront at the edge of the Venetian Lagoon; modest sights.
gem:leicester: Large city with the King Richard III centre, the cathedral and castle remains; a short list of sights, much plain fabric.
gem:vittorio-veneto: Base for the UNESCO Prosecco hills 7 km off and the Revine lakes, with three local museums; a quiet town to sleep in.
gem:lectoure: Gascon hill town on a ridge, with a cathedral and the Carmelite chapel; a pleasant half day, quiet beyond it.
gem:long-eaton: Midlands town with Attenborough Nature Reserve four kilometres off; the town itself is ordinary and offers little to see.
gem:marburg-an-der-lahn: University town rising from the Elisabethkirche to the Landgrafenschloss; a rewarding day, though not a long stay.
gem:lednice: Lednice Castle, its park minaret and Janův hrad in the Lednice-Valtice landscape; a fine day out, the village itself is small.
gem:ablain-saint-nazaire: Village under the Notre-Dame de Lorette war cemetery, with the Vimy Memorial 5 km away; a moving half day, nothing beyond remembrance.
gem:jaujac: Ardèche village in a UNESCO Global Geopark, below volcanic hills; good for walks, few sights of its own.
gem:bad-grund: Harz mining village on the UNESCO water regale, with old adits and a stave church within a few kilometres; very quiet.
gem:wellingborough: Northamptonshire market town with All Hallows church and nearby halls; nothing here to draw a visitor.
gem:gotha: Residence town dominated by the large Friedenstein palace, with a ducal museum and winter palace; strong sights, a quiet town.
gem:castiglione-della-pescaia: Maremma harbour village below its castle, beside the Diaccia Botrona marsh and near Cala Violina; a pleasant beach base, busy in summer.
gem:peterborough: Peterborough Cathedral and the Bronze Age site of Flag Fen are worth a visit; the town around them is largely modern and plain.
gem:turnhout: Flemish town with a begijnhof, a small museum and old churches; a tidy historic centre, but modest for a trip.
gem:asti: Piedmont city with a cathedral, Torre Troyana and a diocesan museum; a quiet provincial centre with no standout sight.
gem:great-yarmouth: Seaside resort town with a minster, a hippodrome and a Roman fort nearby; a beach day out rather than a trip.
gem:le-touquet-paris-plage: Seaside resort of grand villas and a wide beach on the Opal Coast; the UNESCO tag on the card seems wrong.
gem:cangas-do-morrazo: Fishing town on the Ría de Vigo with Rodas and A Lanzada beaches within reach; a good setting, but little to see in town.
gem:camerino: Hilltop university town with a Palazzo Ducale, palaces and old gates, near the Pioraco gorge; quiet and seen in a few hours.
gem:lytham-st-annes: Quiet seaside town with a pier, Lytham Windmill and Lytham Hall, Blackpool's rides 7 km away; pleasant rather than a reason to go.
gem:kilsyth: Former mill town on the UNESCO-listed Antonine Wall, with Bar Hill fort and Colzium Castle; the Roman traces are slight on the ground.
gem:la-cabanasse: High Cerdagne base by the Mont-Louis solar furnace and the Pont Gisclard line; the village itself is plain.
gem:kivik: Skåne fishing village by the Bronze Age King's Grave, with Stenshuvud and Haväng beaches near; a summer stop, small.
gem:burton-upon-trent: Midlands town with abbey remains and a town hall, Tutbury Castle seven kilometres off; little to see for a visitor.
gem:biggleswade: Market town with Saint Andrew's Church and the Shuttleworth Collection nearby; plain streets and little to hold a visitor.
gem:marco-de-canavezes: Small Douro-side town on a tentative heritage list, with an archaeological area and village churches; modest, and quiet.
gem:tenno: Listed hill village above the green Lago di Tenno, with the Varone waterfall and Lake Ledro within reach; small and quiet.
gem:conegliano: Town in UNESCO-listed wine hills, with its castle museum, Duomo and Neptune fountain; a good base for the hills, a modest town.
gem:saint-geniez-d-olt: Listed village on the Lot with a penitents' convent and stately town houses; a short stroll, with little to fill a second visit.
gem:tortona: Piedmont market town with a cathedral, diocesan museum and castle park; pleasant enough, little to fill a day.
gem:meiningen: Thuringian town around Schloss Elisabethenburg and the Staatstheater, with a theatre museum; a compact centre, few other sights.
gem:maury: Village below the castles of Quéribus 4 km and Peyrepertuse 7 km off; a base for the castles, little in the village.
gem:stroud: Cotswold valley mill town with Woodchester Roman Villa 4 km away and commons for walking; little in the centre itself.
gem:stamford: Stone market town with St Leonard's Priory and Burghley House on its edge; a rewarding day, quiet in the evening.
gem:narni: Hill town under the Rocca Albornoziana, with Santa Maria Impensole and the Narni gorge near; a good half day, quiet after.
gem:saltash: Cornish gateway town beside the Royal Albert Bridge and Tamar Bridge, with Plymouth 7 km away; little of its own.
gem:estella-lizarra: Listed town with the Palace of the Kings of Navarre, San Miguel church and Irache monastery close by; a good day, quiet evenings.
gem:zonnebeke: Flanders town at the heart of the Third Battle of Ypres, with cemeteries, memorials and a theme park nearby; sober history stop.
gem:messel: UNESCO fossil pit with a small museum; a site for those interested in fossils, with little else in the village.
gem:battle: Battle Abbey on Senlac Hill, site of the 1066 battle, above a small market street; a half day, then little else.
gem:langres: Walled hill town with a cathedral and an art and history museum, Diderot's birthplace; a good half day, quiet after dark.
gem:montegridolfo: Walled hill village of 154 people in the Borghi più belli list, with north and south walls; tiny, a short walk.
gem:cuellar: Walled Castilian town with its castle, the Pedro I palace and the Jewish quarter gate; quiet, half a day is enough.
gem:kurten: Rural municipality of scattered villages with the Dhünn reservoir and small castles nearby; nothing that draws a visitor.
gem:carmarthen: Welsh county town with castle remains, chapels and a park by the River Towy; a working town with little to hold a visitor.
gem:yeovil: Somerset market town whose best sights lie outside it: Montacute House 6 km, Sherborne Abbey 8 km; little in town itself.
gem:detmold: Open-air museum, the Hermann monument and the Teutoburg Forest close by; the town centre itself is modest.
gem:huesca: Aragonese city with a cathedral, San Pedro el Viejo and a diocesan museum; a quiet provincial centre without a standout.
gem:pickering: Yorkshire market town with Pickering Castle, the church of St Peter and St Paul and its railway station; a pleasant half day.
gem:ipswich: Christchurch Mansion and park and the carved Ancient House stand out; the rest is a workaday county town.
gem:lerici: Borghi più belli harbour town on the Gulf of La Spezia, with Palmaria and Tino islands offshore; few sights in town itself.
gem:ourense: Galician city with a cathedral, a Roman bridge and the hot springs of As Burgas in a listed old quarter; underrated but low-key.
gem:angers: Its château holds the Apocalypse Tapestry, with a cathedral and medieval houses near; a solid day, the wider city is ordinary.
gem:malcesine: Garda lakeshore village under Monte Baldo with a Scaliger castle; a fine base, though busy and one of many lake villages.
gem:ogre: Riverside town with pine hills and dolomite banks, Saint Meinhard Island's church 7 km off; green and quiet, few sights.
gem:torgau: Renaissance Schloss Hartenfels with its Schlosskirche over a well-kept Elbe town; worth a stop, quiet beyond the castle.
gem:benicassim: Beach resort with watchtowers and the Carmelite convent of the Desert de les Palmes in the hills behind; a resort strip first.
gem:cardaillac: Listed village round the Tour de Sagnes, with Figeac's Champollion Museum 8 km away; an hour's walk, little more.
gem:den-helder: Naval port with a navy museum, a submarine, Fort Kijkduin and the Lange Jaap lighthouse; interesting, but a short visit.
gem:montagnana: Walled Veneto town listed among Italy's finest villages, with a roughly 2 km circuit of well-kept medieval walls and towers.
gem:treuchtlingen: Altmühl valley town near Pappenheim castle and the Carolingian Karlsgraben canal; a rail junction more than a place to stay.
gem:keszthely: Balaton lakeside town with the Festetics Palace, and Lake Hévíz 4 km away; a good day, summer-busy and short on old fabric.
gem:requena: Historic-listed town with a medieval walled quarter and old churches; quiet, with a short list of sights.
gem:sommepy-tahure: Champagne battlefield village with a war cemetery and a parish church; moving for First World War visitors, little otherwise.
gem:alassio: Listed Ligurian beach town facing Gallinara island; a lively seafront for a few nights, with little to see beyond the beach.
gem:kleve: Lower Rhine town below the Schwanenburg castle, with the Museum Kurhaus and Schloss Moyland near; pleasant, done in a day.
gem:rottweil: Neckar town with a Holy Cross minster and the Hochturm tower; a tidy historic centre, but a half day is enough.
gem:lleida: La Seu Vella, the old cathedral on its hill, dominates a mostly modern city; one strong sight, little else.
gem:vuillafans: Doubs village on the list of France's most beautiful, with a notable house; Ornans, 7 km away, supplies most of the sights.
gem:vernet-les-bains: Pyrenean spa village at the foot of the Canigó, with Saint-Martin du Canigou abbey and Saint-Michel de Cuxa 6 km away.
gem:norre-vorupor: North Sea fishing village on the edge of Thy National Park, dunes and open beach; bracing and quiet, little to see.
gem:bochum: Ruhr city with the German Mining Museum; industrial heritage and a lively scene, but a plain postwar townscape.
gem:vejle: Fjord city nine kilometres from the Jelling stones and church, with an art museum; a base for Jelling, plain in its own right.
gem:sparta: Modern town with an archaeological museum and the ancient theatre, 5 km from Byzantine Mystras; a base for Mystras more than a sight.
gem:guardamar-del-segura: Spanish resort town with a small castle and old towers near the beaches; mostly a seaside stay, not a sightseeing stop.
gem:scalea: Calabrian beach town with the Talao tower and Dino island 8 km off; summer-led, with little to see outside the coast.
gem:szombathely: West Hungarian city on Roman Savaria, with a baroque cathedral and the Kámon arboretum; a half day, little more.
gem:ullastret: Listed Empordà village with Peratallada 3 km away and Costa Brava coves 12 km off; small, quiet and best as a base.
gem:soko-banja: Serbian spa valley under Ozren with the Soko Grad fortress ruin; restful for a few days, few sights of note.
gem:saint-lary-soulan: Pyrenean valley village at 820 m with old churches and the Pic du Midi within reach; a mountain base, not a sight.
gem:autun: Cathedral, Roman gate and old fountain in a small Burgundy town; rewarding for a day, then little more.
gem:cingoli: Listed hill town at 631 m with Palazzo Castiglioni and an archaeological museum, Lake Cingoli below; a fine view, a short visit.
gem:ciritei: Village on the edge of Piatra Neamț whose sights and museums all lie in that town; nothing of its own to visit.
gem:choustnikovo-hradiste: Small village 3 km from the baroque Kuks Hospital and its Bethlehem carvings in the woods; the sights lie next door, not here.
gem:mondonedo: Listed historic town around Mondoñedo cathedral; a quiet couple of hours with little else nearby.
gem:kelsterbach: Small town on the edge of Frankfurt's airport and industry; the card's sights are neighbouring towns, and nothing invites a stay.
gem:patra: Port city with the Cathedral of Saint Andrew and the Rio–Antirrio bridge nearby; mostly a ferry and transit stop.
gem:kastel: Right-bank suburb of Mainz; the cathedral and Roman theatre on the card lie across the Rhine, the district itself has little.
gem:bialystok: Regional city with the Branicki Palace and its gardens, St Roch's church and the cathedral; a short visit, little to hold you longer.
gem:bad-homburg-vor-der-hohe: Spa town below the Taunus with a castle, Roman Saalburg fort 6 km away and walking; polished rather than memorable.
gem:blankenberge: Belgian seaside resort with a wide beach, marina and the Paravang; a busy holiday front with little old fabric left.
gem:viseu: Portuguese city with a cathedral, remnant walls and the Grão Vasco museum; a calm, handsome centre with modest evening life.
gem:ansbach: Town of the Residenz, the Orangerie and St Gumbertus; a good half day, quiet after.
gem:piacenza: Piazza dei Cavalli with its equestrian statues, the Duomo and Palazzo Farnese; a solid Emilian city, but a day is plenty.
gem:foggia: Apulian city with a cathedral and a theatre; the sights are few and the surroundings flat.
gem:loro-ciuffenna: Valdarno borgo più bello at the foot of the Pratomagno, with the Romanesque Badia di Sant'Andrea; an hour or two, a quiet base.
gem:barletta: The bronze Colossus, a cathedral and a castle on the Adriatic shore; a good half day, little to hold a second.
gem:olsberg: Sauerland town with two small castles and the Bruchhauser Steine rocks 5 km away; a walking base more than a place to see.
gem:szklarska-poreba: Mountain resort below Szrenica with the Kamieńczyk waterfall and Śnieżne Kotły; a hiking base, plain in town.
gem:skalanion: Village outside Heraklion whose named sights, the Archaeological Museum and Koules fort, lie 8 km away in the city; little of its own.
gem:ceaulmont: Creuse valley commune whose listed sights all lie in Argenton, 8 to 10 km away; the village label does not match the card.
gem:spindleruv-mlyn: Giant Mountains resort with the Pančava waterfall, Elbe spring and Sněžka 9 km away; best for walking and skiing.
gem:winterberg: Sauerland upland resort at 679 m below the Kahler Asten, with a panorama bridge; outdoors fun more than a place to see.
gem:vic: Catalan town with its cathedral, the Episcopal Museum and modernist Casa Comella; a good half day, quiet beyond.
gem:le-bonhomme: Vosges village near Lac Blanc with the Tête-des-Faux battlefield; few sights of its own, more a stop than a stay.
gem:hallenberg: Small Sauerland town with several old churches and chapels in green hills; one of many alike, little reason to make the trip.
gem:buonconvento: Listed walled village with a sacred-art museum, the abbey of Monte Oliveto Maggiore 7 km off; small, a good stop rather than a base.
gem:vrnjacka-banja: Serbian spa town with parks and a love bridge; monasteries lie a few kilometres out, the town itself is modest.
gem:rieti: Old town with its cathedral, the Arch of Boniface VIII and the Franciscan way, Fontecolombo 4 km off; a good half day, quiet beyond.
gem:bad-ems: One of the Great Spa Towns of Europe, a spa in a valley with Burg Nassau and Ehrenbreitstein within 8 km; elegant, but quiet.
gem:bad-durkheim: Wine spa town with the Limburg abbey ruins, the Celtic Heidenmauer and Hardenburg castle 4 km away; a good half day, ordinary centre.
gem:kaysersberg: Village below its castle with the Sainte-Croix church, Ribeauvillé and the Hohlandsbourg within 9 km; lovely, but soon walked.
gem:montecatini-terme: One of the Great Spa Towns of Europe, with the Tettuccio baths; elegant and calm, a spa to rest in more than to explore.
gem:segorbe: Listed historic town with its cathedral, Castillo de la Estrella and the Vall de Cristo charterhouse; a half day at most.
gem:sutri: Listed village with a Roman amphitheatre, Lake Vico and Lake Bracciano within reach; a good half day, little after dark.
gem:moret-sur-loing: Listed town on the Loing with its own castle and canal, close to Fontainebleau; handsome and small, so half a day.
gem:tongeren: Limburg town of Roman roots, with the Gallo-Roman Museum and the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwebasiliek; a good day, quiet after.
gem:caen: Castle of Caen, two great abbeys and a fine-arts museum give a solid day; the wider city is plain, the beaches 20 km off.
gem:alta: Arctic town with the UNESCO-listed Rock Art of Alta and the Northern Lights Cathedral; strong sights, a plain modern town.
gem:glorenza: Tiny walled town in South Tyrol, listed among the Borghi più belli, below the Ortler; compact, with little beyond a half day.
gem:chipiona: Andalusian beach town with its own castle and a lone listed sight; the card gives little beyond sand and a seafront.
gem:campobasso: Molise capital with the Castello Monforte above a small old quarter and the Museo Sannitico; a few hours, little more.
gem:lagrasse: Listed medieval village built around the Abbey of Sainte-Marie de Lagrasse; a rewarding half day, small beyond the abbey.
gem:castellane: Alpine village at 727 m with a square tower and a clock tower; Lac de Castillon lies 6 km away.
gem:amboise: Château d'Amboise above the Loire, Clos Lucé and the Chanteloup pagoda in one small town; a full day, busy in summer.
gem:miedzyzdroje: Baltic resort with a long beach and the Kawcza Góra cliff, Wolin National Park 8 km off; a beach town more than a sight.
gem:figeac: Medieval Lot town with the Champollion Museum and old mansions, listed among the finer detours; compact and quiet.
gem:bielefeld: German city with a hilltop fortress and a sculpture park; the centre is largely modern and quickly seen.
gem:bordighera: Riviera town of villas and gardens, with the Lowe gardens and the Ligurian studies institute; pleasant, but a resort more than a sight.
gem:holstebro: West Jutland town with an art museum and town museum; Tvis Abbey lies outside and the centre is modern and plain.
gem:chauvigny: Listed small town with the Bishops' castle, Harcourt castle and the church of Saint-Pierre on its hill; a good half day, quiet beyond.
gem:chambery: Savoy city with a cathedral, a castle and a regional museum, under mountains with Lac du Bourget near; a low-key stay.
gem:norderney: East Frisian island resort with beaches, a lighthouse and a spa theatre; relaxed seaside, but few sights.
gem:ploiesti: Oil city with the Palatul Culturii and a clock museum; a few museums in a largely modern town.
gem:le-croisic: Listed harbour town on a peninsula facing Pen-Bron, the Guérande salt marshes 4 km away; a pleasant stay, few sights of note.
gem:moneglia: Listed seaside village between Punta Baffe and Punta Moneglia, with coast walks and beaches; a calm base, few sights.
gem:grazie: Listed village by the Mincio wetlands, 7 to 8 km from Mantua's Palazzo Te and Camera degli Sposi; the village itself is a short stop.
gem:saint-cyr-sur-mer: Provençal resort with beaches, 15 km from the Calanques coves; a holiday base, little of its own to see.
gem:javea: Costa Blanca town with beaches and coves nearby and a few old fortified houses; mostly a holiday base.
gem:flensburg: Fjord-head harbour city with Saint Nicholas and Saint Mary churches, a brewery and Baltic beaches close by; pleasant, but not large.
gem:wipperfurth: Bergisches Land town by the Bever reservoir, with castles 6 to 8 km off; little to see in the town.
gem:heilbronn: Neckar city whose named sights are a fountain, the station and a power plant; a largely modern centre with little to see.
gem:schwabisch-hall: Old town around St Michael and the Comburg monastery, with the Kunsthalle Würth; a fine town that fills a day, not more.
gem:shtip: North Macedonian town with a Fatih mosque, a clock tower and a bedesten; the card lists no major sight.
gem:bad-kissingen: Spa town on UNESCO's Great Spa Towns of Europe list, with a Kurtheater and castle ruin Botenlauben; a gentle, small-scale centre.
gem:greoux-les-bains: Spa village below its castle, near the Esparron lake and the lower Verdon; a calm base with little of its own.
gem:aviles: Listed old town with the Niemeyer Centre on the estuary and Salinas beach 4 km away; a good day, industrial edges.
gem:pergola: Listed Marche town with the museum of the gilded Roman bronzes and the Chiesa delle Tinte; one museum's worth, then little else.
gem:gliwice: Silesian city with the Radio Tower, a cathedral and a castle; the Guido mine lies 8 km off, the centre is ordinary.
gem:falkenberg: West coast town with an old stone bridge, the church of Sankt Laurentii and a photo museum; a summer stop, little more.
gem:oldenburg: North German city with a palace, the Lappan tower and the Prinzenpalais gallery; a pleasant centre, but no reason to make the trip.
gem:palencia: Listed historic centre led by Palencia Cathedral and its San Antolín crypt; a fine cathedral in a quiet, low-key provincial city.
gem:burghausen: Bavarian town beneath Burg zu Burghausen, with the church of St. Jakob and Raitenhaslach Abbey 6 km off; small beyond the castle.
gem:jonzac: Charente-Maritime town with a castle, listed among the finer detours; churches and Château de Meux lie 6 to 7 km out.
gem:hasselt: Limburg city with St Quentin's cathedral, the Virga-Jesse basilica and the Z33 art house; lively, but a day covers it.
gem:castiglion-fiorentino: Orange-flag hill town with the Cassero tower, collegiate church and art gallery; pleasant for a few hours, little beyond.
gem:les-sables-d-olonne: Atlantic resort with the Armandèche lighthouse and the Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Port church; a beach stay rather than a place to see.
